page: Microsoft Azure F16als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The system provisions 16 dedicated physical cores mapped to 16 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core configuration, operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, complemented by AVX-512 vector support including VNNI and BF16 instructions. Total system memory is 32.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or discrete GPUs, relying on external network storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate superior single-core performance driven by the 4.5 GHz processor clock. The instance achieved top-decile results in Geekbench single-core (2853.0) and multi-core (20959.0) tests, as well as stress-ng single-core processing. Single-threaded data handling is strong, recording 39.02 GB/sec in gzip compression and 17.56 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 114.79 GB/sec and write bandwidth recorded 72.29 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the middle performance tiers. Small model LLM text generation achieved top-tier throughput at 410.65 tokens per second, though lack of high memory prevents hosting large model variants.

The 1:2 memory-to-core configuration provides efficient resource allocation for compute-heavy workloads by eliminating unneeded memory allocations. The absence of local disk drives requires architectural consideration for I/O-intensive workloads, directing disk operations across remote storage. Microsoft Azure F16als_v7 is structured for workloads prioritizing raw CPU throughput, such as software compilation, data compression pipelines, image processing, and high-concurrency microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure F16als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 16-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs running single threads per core and 32.0 GB of system memory, it features a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio suited for compute-intensive tasks. The configuration omits discrete GPUs and bundled local storage, directing disk operations to remote volumes. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core and multi-core capabilities, registering 2853.0 in Geekbench single-core and 39.02 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Uncached large-block memory throughput reaches 114.79 GB/sec for reads, while general database and Redis operations perform in the average tier. The instance eliminates excess memory overhead to deliver dense computing power, making it an efficient choice for build compilation, media transformation, batch compression, and web application serving.
